sources_considered.why: Reproduces the abstract of the peer-reviewed Science paper (July 2023) on ChatGPT productivity effects.

evidence_items.publisher: Science (Noy & Zhang), abstract listed by Stanford SCALE

receipt.public_excerpt: Our results show that ChatGPT substantially raised productivity: The average time taken decreased by 40% and output quality rose by 18%.

evidence_items.explanation: A randomized experiment found ChatGPT cut time on professional writing tasks by 40% and raised quality by 18%. That is a large, practical benefit, and it contradicts 'not particularly useful for anything'.

evidence_items.publisher: National Bureau of Economic Research (Brynjolfsson, Li, Raymond)

receipt.public_excerpt: Access to the tool increases productivity, as measured by issues resolved per hour, by 14% on average, including a 34% improvement for novice and low-skilled workers

evidence_items.explanation: A field study of 5,179 real customer-support agents found a generative AI assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 14%. This is real-world usefulness inside the claim's window.

receipt.public_excerpt: ChatGPT now has 100 million weekly active users, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced on Monday

evidence_items.explanation: Shows large repeat use by late 2023. This is context only, because use does not by itself show usefulness.

unresolved_gaps: No study found that measured the usefulness of DALL-E or other image generators in this period. The contradicting evidence covers text and chat tools.
Both studies use bounded tasks (short writing tasks, customer support). They do not measure economy-wide value.
